empty-page-tree.pdf.reason: A document with no pages has nothing to count or size. pdf.js reports 0 pages and a caller that only checks 'pages <= cap' lets it through. The library fails closed with its own kind, 'empty', separate from 'unparseable': the file is well-formed but has no pages, and a caller may want to tell a damaged upload from an empty one. A wrapper with a fixed set of kinds (such as chatbot-agent's 'pages' | 'pageSize' | 'unparseable' | null) maps 'empty' to 'unparseable'. The test compares the kind, not the message.

Brotli-Prototype-FileA.pdf.reason: The page tree is in a Brotli-compressed object stream. BrotliDecode is a prototype filter, not in ISO 32000-2. The library supports Flate only, so an unknown filter on structure it needs is a failure. Fixture: pdf.js's own test PDFs (bun run samples). See triage-pdfjs-samples.md.

poppler-85140-0.pdf.reason: The page object has an invalid header and declares a MediaBox of 595 x 2147483647; pdf.js reports the Letter default, which hides the declared box. The library never substitutes a size for a page object it cannot parse. A page that parses but has no MediaBox still gets Letter. Fixture: pdf.js's own test PDFs (bun run samples). See triage-pdfjs-samples.md.

bug1250079.pdf.reason: Every dictionary has lost its << and >> delimiters, including the trailer. pdf.js reads it anyway; the library finds no usable trailer and refuses. Stricter, not looser. Fixture: pdf.js's own test PDFs (bun run samples). See triage-pdfjs-samples.md.

PDFBOX-4352-0.pdf.reason: An AES-256 file whose encryption dictionary is corrupted (the opening << is damaged). pdf.js ignores the unreadable dictionary and reads the file as unencrypted; the library refuses, because a file that says it is encrypted and whose encryption cannot be read has not been shown to be readable. Fixture: pdf.js's own test PDFs (bun run samples). See triage-pdfjs-samples.md.
